# AIJ UWE benchmark — cleaned data API

> Wind-tunnel reference data from the Architectural Institute of Japan Urban Wind Environment (UWE)
> benchmark, Cases A-E, cleaned into one schema, plus Eddy3D's validation against it. Static files, plain GET.

Base URL: https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api
Fallback (raw files from the repository): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SustainableUrbanSystemsLab/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/main/docs/api
Repository: https://github.com/SustainableUrbanSystemsLab/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ
API version: 2.0.0. Data version (SHA-256 of the served data): f09f6ec0013369f02ea137ff30f2b53f098a13a5e3952f37b57ab3db1b6f92c7.
Licence: CC-BY-4.0 — the data belongs to its collectors; cite the benchmark and the per-case papers.

## How to use this

1. GET index.json — every endpoint and file (with size and SHA-256), versions, changelog, citation.
2. GET cases.json — the five cases with their frame, units, counts and links. Pick an id (A, B, C, D, E).
3. GET cases/{id}.json — read `frame`, `units` and `known_issues` BEFORE the numbers; they differ per case.
4. GET cases/{id}/points.json (or points.csv) — every value is SI (m, m/s, m^2/s^2) in ONE frame per case;
   unmeasured values are null. Case E's quantity is a dimensionless velocity ratio.
5. GET cases/{id}/geometry.stl — ASCII STL in metres, outward normals, origin at the building / array centre,
   +x along the wind at WD = 0 (Cases A-D). Case E keeps its geographic frame (+x east, +y north, full-scale metres).
   geometry.json lists the boxes where the geometry IS boxes (A, B, C, D), so you need not parse the STL at all.
6. GET validation.json for every case and engine at once, or cases/{id}/validation.json for one case in full.
   Quote the `headline` scores. An engine whose status is not "scored" has NO result for that case: do not
   infer one. "scored" means a run exists, not that it agrees — read the numbers. Each result's `pairs` is
   the per-point measured and modelled values, so any score can be recomputed. Status today: A: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb scored, fluidx3d scored, ml-surrogate scored; B: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb scored, fluidx3d scored, ml-surrogate scored; C: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored; D: openfoam12-realizableKE running, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored; E: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored.
7. All geometry at once: GET geometry.json (every STL with its case, configuration, units, frame and SHA-256)
   or geometry.zip. Each STL stays in its own case's frame and units; they are NOT one scene.
8. Every JSON document names its JSON Schema in `$schema` (schemas/{name}.schema.json); openapi.json describes
   every endpoint. Download URLs carry ?v=<SHA-256 prefix>: use the URLs the documents give, not hand-built ones.
9. Send a descriptive User-Agent: the site's CDN answers HTTP 403 to Python urllib's default one and to some AI
   crawlers. If you are refused, the fallback URL above serves byte-identical files from the repository.

## Endpoints

- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/index.json — every endpoint and file with its size and SHA-256, versions, compatibility policy, changelog, licence, citation
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases.json — the five cases: id, title, frame, units, counts, engine status, links
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}.json — one case in full: configurations, frame, units, inflow fit and approach-flow profile, point-table summary, geometry files, validation status, known data issues, attribution
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/points.json — the cleaned measurement table: SI units, one frame, null where not measured
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/points.csv — the same table as CSV (empty cell = not measured)
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/approach_flow.csv — the measured approach-flow profile: z (m), U (m/s), and k (m^2/s^2) or u_rms (m/s) where published
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/geometry.json — the case's STL files with statistics, renders, and the boxes where the geometry is boxes
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/geometry.stl — cleaned ASCII STL of the default configuration: metres, case frame, outward normals
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/geometry_{configuration}.stl — the other configurations' STLs (C: 0D, 1D; E: bc, before construction)
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/validation.json — Eddy3D's scores per engine and run, with figures and the per-point pairs
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/cases/{id}/pairs/{engine}.csv — per-point measured and modelled values of one engine's runs on the case (columns described by the result's pairs_columns)
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/validation.json — every case and engine in one table: status, runs, headline scores
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/geometry.json — every STL of every case in one list: case, configuration, units, frame, bounding box, size, SHA-256
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/geometry.zip — every STL in one archive (each keeps its own case's frame and units: they are not one scene)
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/schemas/{name}.schema.json — the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of each JSON document
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/openapi.json — OpenAPI 3.1 description of every endpoint
- https://sustainableurbansystems.com/CFD-Test-Cases-Architectural-Institute-of-Japan-AIJ/api/llms.txt — plain-text entry point for agents

## Cases

- A: Case A — 1:1:2 building. Isolated 1:1:2 building, velocity field (split-fibre hot wire). 186 rows, 186 points, columns point_id, config, instrument, wind_direction_deg, x, y, z, U, V, W, uu, vv, ww, k. Engines: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb scored, fluidx3d scored, ml-surrogate scored.
- B: Case B — 1:4:4 slab. Isolated 1:4:4 slab, velocity field (split-fibre hot wire). 224 rows, 224 points, columns point_id, config, instrument, wind_direction_deg, x, y, z, U, V, W, uu, vv, ww, k. Engines: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb scored, fluidx3d scored, ml-surrogate scored.
- C: Case C — 3 × 3 block array. 3 x 3 array of 0.20 m cubes, centre block at 0D / 1D / 2D, pedestrian-height scalar speed (thermistor), 3 wind directions. 1080 rows, 120 points, columns point_id, config, instrument, wind_direction_deg, x, y, z, Vs. Engines: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored.
- D: Case D — high-rise among city blocks. 1:1:4 tower in a regular array of 82 low blocks, pedestrian-height scalar speed (thermistor, 3 wind directions) plus a 33-point split-fibre velocity field at WD = 0. 267 rows, 78 points, columns point_id, config, instrument, wind_direction_deg, x, y, z, U, V, W, uu, vv, ww, k, Vs. Engines: openfoam12-realizableKE running, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored.
- E: Case E — Niigata district. Real district in Niigata at 1:250, before and after a 60 m high-rise and two 18 m mid-rises; pedestrian-height velocity ratio (thermistor), 16 wind directions. 2560 rows, 80 points, columns point_id, config, instrument, wind_direction, wind_direction_deg, x, y, z, velocity_ratio. Engines: openfoam12-realizableKE scored, openlb not comparable, fluidx3d not comparable, ml-surrogate scored.

## Known data issues

Each of these changes the result of a comparison if it is not accounted for.

- [A] Lateral velocity V is positive toward +y (checked: V = -2.893 m/s at (-0.040, -0.050, 0.010), just outside the y < 0 flank, deflecting away from the centreline). Case B uses the OPPOSITE sign; the API flips Case B so both agree.
- [A] Coordinates are metres (Case B's are millimetres in the published file).
- [A] Case A's turbulence columns are rms values (u_rms, ...). The API serves VARIANCES (uu = u_rms^2) so A and B share one column meaning.
- [B] The published coordinates are MILLIMETRES (x[mm]) while velocities are m/s. The API serves metres (coordinate_scale_applied = 0.001). Read as metres, every probe lands 1000x too far out.
- [B] The published lateral velocity V is positive toward -y (V = +3.630 m/s at (-0.025, -0.110, 0.013), just outside the y < 0 flank where the flow must deflect toward -y). The API multiplies V by -1 (lateral_sign_applied = -1) so that V is positive toward +y as in Case A. Scored without this, Case B's V comes out at R = -0.910 against R = +0.959 for U on the same points.
- [B] The RANS solution is symmetric, so model V = 0 on the centre plane while the tunnel measures small non-zero values there.
- [C] The measured quantity Vs is the MEAN OMNIDIRECTIONAL SCALAR speed from a thermistor, not |mean velocity vector|. A RANS |U| is biased low against it; the data paper suggests comparing sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) as a conservative correction (over all 1080 rows no Vs is below 0.13 U_H).
- [C] The 'CB' column is TEXT ('0D', '1D', '2D'); a reader that parses every field as a number gets NaN for it. The header ends with a trailing comma (an empty 8th column).
- [C] 1080 rows = 3 wind directions x 3 centre buildings x 120 points, not 3 configurations. In the 0D configuration the 25 centre grid nodes are still absent although the ground there is free: the grid is held constant across configurations.
- [C] 24 of the 120 points sit exactly on a building face plane (|x| = 0.30 or |y| = 0.30) in the open gap between two blocks: legitimate fluid points, but a probe's cell lookup is delicate there.
- [C] Point numbers 1, 2, 3, 34, 35, 36, 37, 46, 55, 100, 101, 102 do not occur (No. runs 4 ... 132 with nine interior gaps).
- [C] Experimental repeatability, from the mirror-symmetric point pairs: mean |dVs| 0.088-0.137 m/s (0.024-0.038 U_H).
- [D] All of Case D's data lives in LF_caseD.xls, a genuine OLE2/BIFF8 workbook (read it with xlrd 2.x; openpyxl cannot). Sheets: 'Geometry&Points', 'Inflow', 'Results (Exp_S)' (split fibre, WD = 0), 'Results (Exp_T)' (thermistor, 0 / 22.5 / 45 deg).
- [D] Coordinates are millimetres in the workbook; the API serves metres.
- [D] The shipped BD_caseD.stl is dirty: 1572 facets of which 576 are duplicates, and all 83 roofs are wound inward (signed volume 0.011159 m^3 against the true 0.021477 m^3). The API's geometry.stl is rebuilt from the 83 shells' bounding boxes: 996 facets, watertight, volume 0.021477 m^3.
- [D] The thermistor reads a SCALAR speed. Over the 33 points where both instruments overlap at WD = 0, the ratio of mean thermistor speed to mean |U| is 1.342 (the mean of the per-point ratios is 1.50). sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) from the split-fibre data matches the thermistor to FB +0.058, R 0.947; |U| alone to FB +0.292, R 0.872.
- [D] Unmeasured thermistor cells are '-' in the workbook (null here). At WD = 0 the 66 measured values are 33 exact mirror pairs, so only 33 are independent; at 22.5 and 45 deg all 66 are independent.
- [D] A prior Eddy3D comparison kept in the folder (case-d-eddy3d-prior-comparison.xlsx) scores R = +0.096 against the thermistor: a frame or geometry error, not a closure result. It is not a validation.
- [E] The velocity ratio is normalised by the inflow velocity at 15.9 m (= 3.935 m/s), NOT by U_H and NOT by UR = 7.8 m/s. A prior Eddy3D comparison in the folder divided by the wrong reference and came out low by a factor of 2.048 (FAC2 0.338 -> 0.863 once rescaled, R unchanged at 0.661).
- [E] All 2560 published ratios are integer multiples of 0.0198204 (55 distinct levels): the data's own resolution is +/-0.0099, 3.1 % of the median value and about 10 % at the lowest points.
- [E] The readme describes AF_caseE.csv, RS_caseE.csv and BD_caseE.stl, but this repository holds only the .3dm, .ghx, .xls and the MP drawing; everything here is extracted from the workbook and the 3dm.
- [E] case-e.3dm is FULL-SCALE metres (MP_caseE.png is drawn at model scale, +/-0.8 m). Use layers 'buildings' (5,015 meshes, before construction) and 'buildings_new_construction' (3 prisms); exclude the map plate on the Japanese-named general layer, the terrain plates (the site is flat) and 'probes'.
- [E] Do not take the measurement coordinates from the 3dm's 'probes' layer: its 80 spheres sit a median 2.31 m (max 21 m) from the workbook's points, which are authoritative (all 80 fall in open space, min 0.83 m from a building edge).
- [E] The measured quantity is a scalar (thermistor) speed; a RANS |U| is biased low against it in a dense canopy. The construction signal (ac - bc) is largest for SW (mean |d| 0.2155) and smallest for SSE (0.093).

## Validation method

Each case is solved through Eddy3D's production case writer (build-case -> run -> probe), not a hand-built
OpenFOAM case; the probe sits at exactly the tunnel's measurement coordinates. Scores are normalised by U_H
(k by U_H^2; Case E by U at 15.9 m); hit rate uses D = 0.25, W = 0.05 in those units. FAC2 is harsh by
construction on sign-changing V and W; read R and hit rate there. The lateral sign of Case B is corrected
before scoring. Cases C-E measure an omnidirectional SCALAR speed (thermistor): the model is scored as
sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) and as |U|, the two ends of the bracket the measurement must fall in.
The ML surrogate predicts |U|/U_ref at 1.8 m; each case is scaled so its measurement plane lands there.
On the full prediction window it does not respond to the wind direction at all (reversing the wind changes
the field by < 1e-4 U_ref) — its scores grade the geometry it was given, not a wind it was told.

Comprehensive Experimental Database for Validating CFD Simulations in Urban Wind Environment: Benchmark Cases Curated by the Architectural Institute of Japan. Japan Architectural Review 9(1), e70083. https://doi.org/10.1002/2475-8876.70083
- Tominaga, Y., Mochida, A., Yoshie, R., Kataoka, H., Nozu, T., Yoshikawa, M., Shirasawa, T. (2008). AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings. J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn. 96, 1749-1761. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jweia.2008.02.058
- Each case's own requested citation and Zenodo DOI are in cases/{id}.json.
